label: SYNTHETIC READER: a test instrument, never a reader. Fictional; not evidence about the book; not readership.

findings.quote: a register for every number, a check every change passes, a site to work on
findings.why: The four pipes are a strong takeaway for a busy reader, but the brief and its file are only named here and never say what to start with on Monday until the very end.

findings.quote: Put the two side by side and half of the page is the check said in words.
findings.why: It instructs the reader to do an exercise with a chapter 4 card they may not have in front of them on a phone.

findings.quote: every link resolves; every page has its plain-text twin; no code loaded from elsewhere
findings.why: A conference team reads a list of site-specific checks and cannot tell which ones apply to a stand and talks, and 'plain-text twin' is unexplained.

findings.quote: None of the three made it into the talk. It was not luck, it was the register doing its job
findings.why: Short declaratives stacked before the lesson; the thought could run in one sentence.

findings.quote: Chapter 5 has the example I like best: on the first night, the check stopped the release
findings.why: It points to an example told elsewhere and gives only the punchline here, so the reader gets neither the story nor a reason to turn back.

findings.quote: 53 files at the end of the first hour, 1,313 at the day's last release
findings.why: The text reads out the figure the growth chart then draws, and the numbers do little for a team deciding whether to copy this.

findings.quote: The last pipe is the simplest, and on the day it was the one that did not quite work.
findings.why: Good, but the following lines return to reporting the files with no I and no hindsight about what he would do now.

findings.quote: The rule was right, and nobody used it, me included.
findings.why: A neat triad of short beats; it lands, but the chapter ends on failure with the fix held back in a team note.

findings.quote: For nine hours the team had worked on its own; now the day starts to accelerate.
findings.why: For a reader worried about needing one central person, the chapter title and this opening make the editor the hero, and the method looks like it depends on him coming back.

findings.quote: Everything in this chapter is on the way to it.
findings.why: It tells the reader how to read the chapter before the reader has any reason to care about the player.

findings.quote: That failure stays in the book.
findings.why: A short declarative closing a run of short sentences; the admission is stronger if folded into the thought before it.

findings.quote: The checks did not soften because I was in the room. That is what they are for.
findings.why: A 'that is the point' style closer that explains the moral the scene had already shown.

findings.quote: That was the moment the team stopped waiting for me and started keeping up with me.
findings.why: It again centres one person as the bottleneck, which is the deal-breaker for a team with an agent each.

findings.quote: That is the whole idea of this book in one commit
findings.why: A large claim the reader cannot yet weigh, since the ruv.sgit.ai experiment was never explained.

findings.quote: It looks a lot like an OODA loop, and maybe it is a variation on it
findings.why: OODA is used without a gloss, and a busy practical reader will stall or skip.

findings.quote: The line is the honest heart of a map like that: it shows you where things are
findings.why: It ranks the line as honest and tells the reader what to take from it, where the maps themselves are never shown in words.

findings.quote: It "does not hold. The data says the opposite"
findings.why: The finding is quoted, then restated two paragraphs later as the researcher saying the line did not hold.

findings.quote: If you think I was wrong, the researcher's sources are in the register, and you can check.
findings.why: A useful invitation, but this reader has no access to the register on a phone and the actual claim is never stated plainly enough to judge.

what_holds: 11-the-plumbing.md: four pipes as a copyable starting kit (register, check, site, brief) and the admission that the corrections file stayed at 'None yet'.
12-the-creator-comes-back.md: the conductor refusing to write into other members' folders while the editor stood there, which is the part a team could copy.
13-the-story-before-the-slides.md: asking an agent to argue against the plan in writing while the person still decides, a one-line takeaway I would try tomorrow.
notes: Overall practical and usable. Main worry for this persona is that chapters 12 and 13 lean on the editor as the one decision point; the Something to try cards are the best part and could come earlier.
